sanskrit_shloka: ॐ नमस्ते रुद्र मन्यव उतोत इषवे नमः, नमस्ते अस्तु धन्वने बाहुभ्यामुत ते नमः.
transliteration: ōm namaste rudra manyava utota iṣave namaḥ, namaste astu dhanvane bāhubhyāmuta te namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Thee, Rudra; prostration to Thy wrath and Thy arrow (which destroy evil); prostration to Thy bow; prostration to Thy mighty Arms.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Thee, Rudra; prostration to Thy wrath and Thy arrow (which destroy evil); prostration to Thy bow; prostration to Thy mighty Arms.

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—According to the celebrated Sayana Acharya, the Rudra chapter of the Yajur Veda consists of the mantras by which oblations are offered in the Sacrifice of Knowledge, wherein the manifold universe is visualised as the extensive manifestation of the Supreme Being.

sanskrit_shloka: या त इषुः शिवतमा शिवꣳ बभूव ते धनुः, शिवा शरव्या या तव तया नो रुद्र मृडय.
transliteration: yā ta iṣuḥ śivatamā śivaṁ babhūva te dhanuḥ, śivā śaravyā yā tava tayā no rudra mṛḍaya.
translation: This, Thy arrow that has become exceedingly peaceful (to the devout); Thy bow become a source of auspiciousness, and Thy quiver of blessedness; with these, O Valiant One (Rudra), make us happy.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: This, Thy arrow that has become exceedingly peaceful (to the devout); Thy bow become a source of auspiciousness, and Thy quiver of blessedness; with these, O Valiant One (Rudra), make us happy.

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—While the first mantra invokes the Terrible Power for destruction of evil, the second envisages the fulfilment of the arms on the establishment of peace, and the now benignant phase of what was once formidable.

sanskrit_shloka: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूरघोराऽपापकाशिनी, तया नस्तनुवा शन्तमया गिरिशꣳताभिचाकशीहि.
transliteration: yā te rudra śivā tanūraghorā'pāpakāśinī, tayā nastanuvā śantamayā giriśaṁtābhicākaśīhi.
translation: Rudra! That blessed and benign form of Thine, which obliterates the trace of all sins—with that most hallowed and calm phase of Thy being, reveal Thyself to us, O Radiator of Peace from the Mount of Kailasa!

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Rudra! That blessed and benign form of Thine, which obliterates the trace of all sins—with that most hallowed and calm phase of Thy being, reveal Thyself to us, O Radiator of Peace from the Mount of Kailasa!

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—Rudra-Siva is said to have two forms, the terrific and the beatific, which are manifested at different times.

sanskrit_shloka: यामिषुꣳ गिरिशꣳत हस्ते बिभर्ष्यस्तवे, शिवाꣳ गिरित्र ताꣳ कुरु मा हिग्ꣳसीः पुरुषꣳ जगत्.
transliteration: yāmiṣuṁ giriśaṁta haste bibharṣyastave, śivāṁ giritra tāṁ kuru mā higṁsīḥ puruṣaṁ jagat.
translation: O Benefactor from the Mount of Kailasa! That arrow which Thou wieldest for aiming at enemies, make that benign (in respect of us). Harm not human beings or others in creation, O Protector on the sacred Mount!

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: O Benefactor from the Mount of Kailasa! That arrow which Thou wieldest for aiming at enemies, make that benign (in respect of us). Harm not human beings or others in creation, O Protector on the sacred Mount!

sanskrit_shloka: शिवेन वचसा त्वा गिरिशाच्छावदामसि, यथा नः सर्वमिज्जगदयक्ष्मग्ꣳसुमना असत्.
transliteration: śivena vacasā tvā giriśācchāvadāmasi, yathā naḥ sarvamijjagadayakṣmagṁsumanā asat.
translation: Resident of the Mountains! We pray to Thee with auspicious eulogies for the sake of attaining Thee. Do so deign that this whole world of ours is rid of all ailment and affliction, and blooms with a joyous mind.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Resident of the Mountains! We pray to Thee with auspicious eulogies for the sake of attaining Thee. Do so deign that this whole world of ours is rid of all ailment and affliction, and blooms with a joyous mind.

sanskrit_shloka: अध्यवोचदधिवक्ता प्रथमो दैव्यो भिषक्, अहीग्ꣳश्च सर्वाञ्जꣳभयन्त्सर्वाश्च यातुधान्यः.
transliteration: adhyavocadadhivaktā prathamo daivyo bhiṣak, ahīgṁśca sarvāñjaṁbhayantsarvāśca yātudhānyaḥ.
translation: May that Divine Physician, First among gods, exalt me in His all-redeeming Transcendent Being, having cut off all evil, whether in the form of poisonous creatures and wild beasts, or the demoniacal natures in creation.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: May that Divine Physician, First among gods, exalt me in His all-redeeming Transcendent Being, having cut off all evil, whether in the form of poisonous creatures and wild beasts, or the demoniacal natures in creation.

sanskrit_shloka: असौ यस्ताम्रो अरुण उत बभ्रुः सुमꣳगलः, ये चेमाग्ꣳरुद्रा अभितो दिक्षु श्रिताः सहस्रशोऽवैषाग्ꣳहेड ईमहे.
transliteration: asau yastāmro aruṇa uta babhruḥ sumaṁgalaḥ, ye cemāgṁrudrā abhito dikṣu śritāḥ sahasraśo'vaiṣāgṁheḍa īmahe.
translation: This (Rudra in the form of the Sun), ruddy, pink, brownish and yellow and of variegated hue (in different stages of rising from the horizon), most auspicious (being dispeller of darkness), manifested in the bright rays enveloping (the earth) from all directions, ranging in tens and thousands—we mitigate the penetrating ferocity of these with our prostrations.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: This (Rudra in the form of the Sun), ruddy, pink, brownish and yellow and of variegated hue (in different stages of rising from the horizon), most auspicious (being dispeller of darkness), manifested in the bright rays enveloping (the earth) from all directions, ranging in tens and thousands—we mitigate the penetrating ferocity of these with our prostrations.

sanskrit_shloka: असौ योऽवसर्पति नीलग्रीवो विलोहितः उतैनꣳ गोपा अदृशन्नदृशन्नुदहार्यः उतैनꣳ विश्वाभूतानि स दृष्टो मृडयाति नः.
transliteration: asau yo’vasarpati nīlagrīvo vilohitaḥ utainaṁ gopā adṛśannadṛśannudahāryaḥ utainaṁ viśvābhūtāni sa dṛṣṭo mṛḍayāti naḥ.
translation: This Blue-necked (due to drinking poison), Red-complexioned One, who traverses through the sky (in the form of the Sun)—Him do see (with their eyes) the unlettered cowherds as well as the maids carrying water, Him do also see all beings (both high and low). May He (Rudra) make us happy.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: This Blue-necked (due to drinking poison), Red-complexioned One, who traverses through the sky (in the form of the Sun)—Him do see (with their eyes) the unlettered cowherds as well as the maids carrying water, Him do also see all beings (both high and low). May He (Rudra) make us happy.

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—The import of this mantra is that while the Lord as seated in such regions as Mount Kailasa is accessible only to those who have spiritual realisation, as the Sun He is visible to everyone. In His great compassion He makes Himself felt even by our outer senses.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो अस्तु नीलग्रीवाय सहस्राक्षाय मीढुषे, अथो ये अस्य सत्वानोऽहꣳ तेभ्योऽकरन्नमः.
transliteration: namo astu nīlagrīvāya sahasrākṣāya mīḍhuṣe, atho ye asya satvāno'haṁ tebhyo'karannamaḥ.
translation: Salutation be to Nilagriva (with blue neck), who has a thousand eyes (as Indra), and who pours down (as rain or parjanya); salutation be from me to others, too, who attend upon Him (as His servants).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Salutation be to Nilagriva (with blue neck), who has a thousand eyes (as Indra), and who pours down (as rain or parjanya); salutation be from me to others, too, who attend upon Him (as His servants).

sanskrit_shloka: प्रमुꣳच धन्वनस्त्व-मुभयो-रार्त्नियोर्ज्याम्, याश्चते हस्त इषवः परा ता भगवो व.
transliteration: pramuṁca dhanvanastva-mubhayo-rārtniyorjyām, yāścate hasta iṣavaḥ parā tā bhagavo va.
translation: Lord! Unfurl the string at both the ends of Thy bow. Those arrows that are in Thy hand, set them aside (now, after the enemy has been destroyed).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Lord! Unfurl the string at both the ends of Thy bow. Those arrows that are in Thy hand, set them aside (now, after the enemy has been destroyed).

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—The term ‘Lord’ is the equivalent of the Sanskrit original ‘Bhagavan’, which means one who is possessed of all wealth (Aisvarya), valour (Virya), fame (Yasas), prosperity (Shri), wisdom (Jnana), nonattachment to things (Vairagya)—an epithet of the Almighty.

sanskrit_shloka: अवतत्य धनुस्त्वगीसहस्राक्ष शतेषुधे, निशीर्य शल्यानाꣳ मुखा शिवो नः सुमना भव.
transliteration: avatatya dhanustvagïsahasrākṣa śateṣudhe, niśīrya śalyānāṁ mukhā śivo naḥ sumanā bhava.
translation: O Thousand-eyed Divinity! Thou that hast hundreds of quivers (in war)! Setting down Thy bow, and dismantling the ends of Thy piercing arrows (after Thy purpose has been fulfilled), become Thou auspiciousness unto us, with a charming mood of blessing.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: O Thousand-eyed Divinity! Thou that hast hundreds of quivers (in war)! Setting down Thy bow, and dismantling the ends of Thy piercing arrows (after Thy purpose has been fulfilled), become Thou auspiciousness unto us, with a charming mood of blessing.

sanskrit_shloka: विज्यꣳ धनुः कपर्दिनो विशल्यो बाणवागीउत, अनेशन्नस्येषव आभुरस्य निषꣳगथिः.
transliteration: vijyaṁ dhanuḥ kapardino viśalyo bāṇavāgïuta, aneśannasyeṣava ābhurasya niṣaṁgathiḥ.
translation: May the bow of Kapardin (Siva) be freed from its string; and may His quiver be without the piercing ends of the arrows held above. May his arrows become incapable of piercing through, and may His bow become merely a support for the arrows (and not to shoot them). Note:—This mantra and the others which pray for the putting down of the weapons of Rudra-Siva are invocations of His peaceful aspect, which manifests itself when He is not engaged in the work of destruction with His fierce arms.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: May the bow of Kapardin (Siva) be freed from its string; and may His quiver be without the piercing ends of the arrows held above. May his arrows become incapable of piercing through, and may His bow become merely a support for the arrows (and not to shoot them). Note:—This mantra and the others which pray for the putting down of the weapons of Rudra-Siva are invocations of His peaceful aspect, which manifests itself when He is not engaged in the work of destruction with His fierce arms.

sanskrit_shloka: या ते हेतिर्मीढुष्टम हस्ते बभूव ते धनुः, तयाऽस्मान्विश्वतस्त्व-मयक्ष्मया परिब्भुज.
transliteration: yā te hetirmīḍhuṣṭama haste babhūva te dhanuḥ, tayā'smānviśvatastva-mayakṣmayā paribbhuja.
translation: O Abundant Source of all fulfilments! Protect us Thou, from all sides, with the weapons (like the sword) and the bow in Thy hands, that have ceased from purposes of destruction.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: O Abundant Source of all fulfilments! Protect us Thou, from all sides, with the weapons (like the sword) and the bow in Thy hands, that have ceased from purposes of destruction.

sanskrit_shloka: नमस्ते अस्त्वायुधायानातताय धृष्णवे, उभाभ्यामुत ते नमो बाहुभ्याꣳ तव धन्वने.
transliteration: namaste astvāyudhāyānātatāya dhṛṣṇave, ubhābhyāmuta te namo bāhubhyāṁ tava dhanvane.
translation: Salutation be to Thy weapon arrow that has not been extended on the bow, but is capable of striking the enemy! Salutation to Thy bow. And salutation to Thy two arms.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Salutation be to Thy weapon arrow that has not been extended on the bow, but is capable of striking the enemy! Salutation to Thy bow. And salutation to Thy two arms.

sanskrit_shloka: परि ते धन्वनो हेतिरस्मान्व्रुणक्तु विश्वतः, अथो य इषुधिस्तवारे अस्मन्निधेहि तम्.
transliteration: pari te dhanvano hetirasmānvruṇaktu viśvataḥ, atho ya iṣudhistavāre asmannidhehi tam.
translation: Lord! May the pointed arrows of thy bow exclude us in every way (from their destructive operations). And that quiver of Thine, may Thou keep it far away from us (and protect us).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Lord! May the pointed arrows of thy bow exclude us in every way (from their destructive operations). And that quiver of Thine, may Thou keep it far away from us (and protect us).

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—According to another interpretation, the second line can be rendered thus: ‘And that quiver of Thine, may Thou direct it to our enemies.’

sanskrit_shloka: ॐ नमस्ते अस्तु भगवन् विश्वेश्वराय महादेवाय त्र्यꣳबकाय त्रिपुरान्तकाय त्रिकलाग्नि-कालाय कालाग्निरुद्राय नीलकण्ठाय म्रुत्युꣳजयाय सर्वेश्वराय शन्करय सदाशिवाय श्रीमन्महादेवाय नमः.
transliteration: ōm namaste astu bhagavan viśveśvarāya mahādevāya tryaṁbakāya tripurāntakāya trikalāgni-kālāya kālāgnirudrāya nīlakaṇṭhāya mrutyuṁjayāya sarveśvarāya śankaraya sadāśivāya śrīmanmahādevāya namaḥ.
translation: Prostration be to Thee, O Lord, Ruler of the universe, Great God Three-Eyed One, Destroyer of the Tripuras, Death to the destructive Fire of the three worlds at the end of Time, Terror to even to the terrible Fire of Time, Blue-necked One, Overcomer of mortality, Overlord over everyone, Bestower of Blessedness, Ever-Auspicious, the Blessed Great God—to Thee, prostration.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration be to Thee, O Lord, Ruler of the universe, Great God Three-Eyed One, Destroyer of the Tripuras, Death to the destructive Fire of the three worlds at the end of Time, Terror to even to the terrible Fire of Time, Blue-necked One, Overcomer of mortality, Overlord over everyone, Bestower of Blessedness, Ever-Auspicious, the Blessed Great God—to Thee, prostration.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो हिरण्यबाहवे सेनान्ये दिशाꣳ च पतये नमो नमो वृक्षेभ्यो हरिकेशेभ्यः पशूनाꣳ पतये नमो नमः सस्पिञ्जराय त्विषीमते पथीनाꣳ पतये नमः.
transliteration: namo hiraṇyabāhave senānye diśāṁ ca pataye namo namo vṛkṣebhyo harikeśebhyaḥ paśūnāṁ pataye namo namaḥ saspiñjarāya tviṣīmate pathīnāṁ pataye namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to the Golden-armed One, the Supreme Commander of all forces, the Lord of all quarters. Prostration to the Vital Essence and Source of the green-leafed trees, the Master of all created beings. Prostration to the Self-effulgent One, the Lord of the different routes (which souls take on departure from this world).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Golden-armed One, the Supreme Commander of all forces, the Lord of all quarters. Prostration to the Vital Essence and Source of the green-leafed trees, the Master of all created beings. Prostration to the Self-effulgent One, the Lord of the different routes (which souls take on departure from this world).

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—In the first section, the Rudra-Adhyaya delineated the Power of Rudra-Siva in His form as the Wielder of the bow and arrows. In the subsequent sections, His glories as revealed in all creation, as manifest in every quarter and cranny, are described. These hymns abound in a varied adoration of the Supreme Being in all things, and every word of ‘prostration’ is repeated twice, as prostration on both sides, and prostration in the beginning and in the end (which is avoided in the translation).

sanskrit_shloka: नमो बभ्लुशाय विव्याधिनेऽन्नानाꣳ पतये नमो नमो हरिकेशायोपवीतिने पुष्टानाꣳ पतये नमो नमो भवस्य हेत्यै जगताꣳ पतये नमो.
transliteration: namo babhluśāya vivyādhine'nnānāṁ pataye namo namo harikeśāyopavītine puṣṭānāṁ pataye namo namo bhavasya hetyai jagatāṁ pataye namo.
translation: Prostration to the Rider of the bull, the Chastiser of the opposing force, the Lord of food or Ruler over matter. Prostration to the One with blue hair on the head (not turned gray), the Wearer of the sacred thread (indicating auspiciousness), the Master of those who are full with the qualities of perfection. Prostration to the Severer of samsara, the Sovereign over all creation.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Rider of the bull, the Chastiser of the opposing force, the Lord of food or Ruler over matter. Prostration to the One with blue hair on the head (not turned gray), the Wearer of the sacred thread (indicating auspiciousness), the Master of those who are full with the qualities of perfection. Prostration to the Severer of samsara, the Sovereign over all creation.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो रुद्रायातताविने क्षेत्राणाꣳ पतये नमो नमः सूतायाहन्त्याय वनानाꣳ पतये नमो नमः रोहिताय स्थपतये वृक्षाणाꣳ पतये नमः.
transliteration: namo rudrāyātatāvine kṣetrāṇāṁ pataye namo namaḥ sūtāyāhantyāya vanānāṁ pataye namo namaḥ rohitāya sthapataye vṛkṣāṇāṁ pataye namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Rudra, who protects with His outstretched bow, the Ruler of all fields (temples, bodies and all creation). Prostration to the Charioteer (Director of all things), the Invincible One, the Lord of all

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Rudra, who protects with His outstretched bow, the Ruler of all fields (temples, bodies and all creation). Prostration to the Charioteer (Director of all things), the Invincible One, the Lord of all

sanskrit_shloka: फ़ोरेस्त्स् (वेगेततिओन् लिफ़े).
transliteration: forests (vegetation life).
translation: Prostration to the crimson-hued One, who, existing (even) in trees, is the Supreme Protector of all.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the crimson-hued One, who, existing (even) in trees, is the Supreme Protector of all.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो मन्त्रिणे वाणिजाय कक्षाणाꣳ पतये नमो नमो भुवꣳतये वारिवस्कृतायौषधीनाꣳ पतये नमो नम उच्चैर्घोषायाक्रन्दयते पत्तीनाꣳ पतये नमो नमः कृत्स्नवीताय धावते सत्वनाꣳ पतये नमः.
transliteration: namo mantriṇe vāṇijāya kakṣāṇāṁ pataye namo namo bhuvaṁtaye vārivaskṛtāyauṣadhīnāṁ pataye namo nama uccairghoṣāyākrandayate pattīnāṁ pataye namo namaḥ kṛtsnavītāya dhāvate satvanāṁ pataye namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to the One who manifests Himself as the minister in a royal court, as the merchant in business, and as the ruler over all the plant kingdom; prostration to the Creator of the world, the Master of all wealth, the Lord over medicines; prostration to Him who thunders in battle and makes the enemy shriek in fear, and is the Commander of all forces; prostration to the All-enveloping One, the Fast in action, the Refuge of the self-surrendering devotees.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the One who manifests Himself as the minister in a royal court, as the merchant in business, and as the ruler over all the plant kingdom; prostration to the Creator of the world, the Master of all wealth, the Lord over medicines; prostration to Him who thunders in battle and makes the enemy shriek in fear, and is the Commander of all forces; prostration to the All-enveloping One, the Fast in action, the Refuge of the self-surrendering devotees.

sanskrit_shloka: नमः सहमानाय निव्याधिन आव्याधिनीनाꣳ पतये नमो नमः ककुभाय निषङ्गिणे स्तेनानाꣳ पतये नमः.
transliteration: namaḥ sahamānāya nivyādhina āvyādhinīnāṁ pataye namo namaḥ kakubhāya niṣaṅgiṇe stenānāṁ pataye namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to the valiant Confronter of foes; the terrific Uprooter of the opposing forces, the Protector of the powers (of dharma) pressing from all sides; prostration to the Lord seated on the hump of the bull, armed with the sword, the Chief of (even) thieves (or stealer of everyone’s heart).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the valiant Confronter of foes; the terrific Uprooter of the opposing forces, the Protector of the powers (of dharma) pressing from all sides; prostration to the Lord seated on the hump of the bull, armed with the sword, the Chief of (even) thieves (or stealer of everyone’s heart).

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—The appellation ‘Chief of thieves’ is to indicate the supreme immanence and the non-exclusiveness of the Divine Being.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो निषङ्गिण इषुधिमते तस्कराणाꣳ पतये नमो नमो वञ्चते परिवञ्चते स्तायूनाꣳ पतये नमो नमो निचेरवे परिचरायारण्यानाꣳ पतये नमो.
transliteration: namo niṣaṅgiṇa iṣudhimate taskarāṇāṁ pataye namo namo vañcate parivañcate stāyūnāṁ pataye namo namo nicerave paricarāyāraṇyānāṁ pataye namo.
translation: Prostration to the Chief of robbers, to Him who is armed with quiver and arrows; prostration to the deceiving, the tricky and elusive Lord of marauders; prostration to the ever-cunning Leader of the thieves lurking at home and those wandering in the streets and the forests. Note:—The Lord is adored as the Chief of thieves, etc., in two senses. Firstly, He is the indwelling presence of even the thieves, and their lives are impossible without His existence in them as their essence. Secondly, He is also the jiva, which is the thief, apart from His being Isvara ranging beyond the realm of the former. Also, the Lord it is that sports as the high and low, the good and the bad, the virtuous and the debased, when looked at from the standpoint of the universe taken as a whole, a view which is hard for the jiva sunk in personalistic cognitions and perceptions but the right vision of those who are absorbed in Reality. Ethical concepts stand transfigured in the Absolute. These mantras of the Veda are to help the seeker in recognising God through the medium of all creation.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Chief of robbers, to Him who is armed with quiver and arrows; prostration to the deceiving, the tricky and elusive Lord of marauders; prostration to the ever-cunning Leader of the thieves lurking at home and those wandering in the streets and the forests. Note:—The Lord is adored as the Chief of thieves, etc., in two senses. Firstly, He is the indwelling presence of even the thieves, and their lives are impossible without His existence in them as their essence. Secondly, He is also the jiva, which is the thief, apart from His being Isvara ranging beyond the realm of the former. Also, the Lord it is that sports as the high and low, the good and the bad, the virtuous and the debased, when looked at from the standpoint of the universe taken as a whole, a view which is hard for the jiva sunk in personalistic cognitions and perceptions but the right vision of those who are absorbed in Reality. Ethical concepts stand transfigured in the Absolute. These mantras of the Veda are to help the seeker in recognising God through the medium of all creation.

sanskrit_shloka: नमः सृकाविभ्यो जिघागीसद्भ्यो मुष्णताꣳ पतये नमो नमोऽसिमद्भ्यो नक्त ꣳचरद्भ्यः प्रकृन्तानाꣳ पतये नमो नम उ ष्णीषिणे गिरिचराय कुलुञ्चानाꣳ पतये नमः.
transliteration: namaḥ sṛkāvibhyo jighāgïsadbhyo muṣṇatāṁ pataye namo namo'simadbhyo nakta ṁcaradbhyaḥ prakṛntānāṁ pataye namo nama u ṣṇīṣiṇe giricarāya kuluñcānāṁ pataye namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to the Chief of the self-protecting animals and of the retaliating thieves ever ready to strike people to death; prostration to the Chief of dacoits, armed with swords and prowling in the night for booty; prostration to the roving Chief with helmet and turban, wandering through the mountains, who steals away people ’s belongings in houses and fields.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Chief of the self-protecting animals and of the retaliating thieves ever ready to strike people to death; prostration to the Chief of dacoits, armed with swords and prowling in the night for booty; prostration to the roving Chief with helmet and turban, wandering through the mountains, who steals away people ’s belongings in houses and fields.

sanskrit_shloka: नम इषुमद्भ्यो धन्वाविभ्यश्च वो नमो नम आतन्वानेभ्यः प्रतिदधानेभ्यश्च वो नमो नम आयच्छद्भ्यो विसृजद्भ्यश्च वो नमो नमोऽस्यद्भ्यो विद्ध्यद्भ्य श्च वो नमो नमः.
transliteration: nama iṣumadbhyo dhanvāvibhyaśca vo namo nama ātanvānebhyaḥ pratidadhānebhyaśca vo namo nama āyacchadbhyo visṛjadbhyaśca vo namo namo'syadbhyo viddhyadbhya śca vo namo namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in the forms of those that move about holding bows and using arrows; prostration to Him who is in those that string their bows and discharge the arrows; prostration to Him who is in those that stretch the bows and send arrows again; prostration to Him who is in those that shoot the arrows and make them hit the targets.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in the forms of those that move about holding bows and using arrows; prostration to Him who is in those that string their bows and discharge the arrows; prostration to Him who is in those that stretch the bows and send arrows again; prostration to Him who is in those that shoot the arrows and make them hit the targets.

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note: —The great commentator Sayana makes a suggestive hint that the forms are all ‘Rudras’, which implies the startling truth that the contents of the world are all God Himself—not that He is merely present in them.

sanskrit_shloka: नम आसीनेभ्यशशायानेभ्यश्च वो नमो नम ःस्वपद्भ्यो जाग्रद्भ्यश्च वो नमो नमस्ति ष्ठद्भ्यो धावद्भ्यश्च वो नमो नम ःसभाभ्यः सभापतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो अ श्वेभ्योऽश्वपतिभ्यश्च वो नमः.
transliteration: nama āsīnebhyaśaśāyānebhyaśca vo namo nama ḥsvapadbhyo jāgradbhyaśca vo namo namasti ṣṭhadbhyo dhāvadbhyaśca vo namo nama ḥsabhābhyaḥ sabhāpatibhyaśca vo namo namo a śvebhyo'śvapatibhyaśca vo namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Thee who art the sitting and the reclining; prostration to Thee who art the sleeping and the waking; prostration to Thee who art the standing (static) and the running (dynamic); prostration to Thee who art the assemblies and the assembly chiefs; prostration to Thee who art the horses and the horse riders.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Thee who art the sitting and the reclining; prostration to Thee who art the sleeping and the waking; prostration to Thee who art the standing (static) and the running (dynamic); prostration to Thee who art the assemblies and the assembly chiefs; prostration to Thee who art the horses and the horse riders.

sanskrit_shloka: नम आव्यधिनीभ्यो विविध्यन्तीभ्यश्च वो नमो नम उग णाभ्यस्तृगीहतीभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो ग् ऋत्सेभ्यो गृत्सपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो व्र् आतेभ्यो व्रातपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमः.
transliteration: nama āvyadhinībhyo vividhyantībhyaśca vo namo nama uga ṇābhyastṛgïhatībhyaśca vo namo namo g ṛtsebhyo gṛtsapatibhyaśca vo namo namo vr ātebhyo vrātapatibhyaśca vo namo namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) the Saktis competent to strike all round in various ways; prostration to Thee who art the gentle higher Saktis as well as the violent lower Saktis; prostration to Thee who art those that run after sense-pleasures as also their leaders; prostration to Thee who art the hosts of (living and non-living) beings as well as their chiefs.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) the Saktis competent to strike all round in various ways; prostration to Thee who art the gentle higher Saktis as well as the violent lower Saktis; prostration to Thee who art those that run after sense-pleasures as also their leaders; prostration to Thee who art the hosts of (living and non-living) beings as well as their chiefs.

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note: —The word ‘Sakti’ does not occur in the original, but is used in the translation to bring out the significance of the feminine gender of the words in the mantra, which indicate the various Saktis or Powers of the Lord. Sayana states that the gentle ones are the seven Matrikas, etc, while the violent ones are Durga, etc.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो गणेभ्यो गणपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो विर् ऊपेभ्यो विश्वरूपेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो महद्भ्य ःक्षुल्लकेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो रथिभ्योऽरथेभ्य श्च वो नमो नमो रथेभ्यो रथपतिभ्य श्च वो नमः.
transliteration: namo gaṇebhyo gaṇapatibhyaśca vo namo namo vir ūpebhyo viśvarūpebhyaśca vo namo namo mahadbhya ḥkṣullakebhyaśca vo namo namo rathibhyo'rathebhya śca vo namo namo rathebhyo rathapatibhya śca vo namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) the hosts of celestial attendants and their chiefs; prostration to Thee who art the formless and the universal-formed; prostration to Thee who art the great as well as the small; prostration to Thee who art those that ride in chariots and those that do not; prostration to Thee who art the chariots as well as the chariot owners.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) the hosts of celestial attendants and their chiefs; prostration to Thee who art the formless and the universal-formed; prostration to Thee who art the great as well as the small; prostration to Thee who art those that ride in chariots and those that do not; prostration to Thee who art the chariots as well as the chariot owners.

sanskrit_shloka: नमः सेनाभ्यः सेननिभ्यश्च वो नमो नम ःक्षत्तृभ्यः सꣳग्रहीतृभ्यश्च वो नमो नमस्तक्षभ्यो रथकारेभ्यश्च वो नमो नम ःकुलालेभ्यः कमारेभ्यश्च वो नमो नम ःपुञ्जिष्टेभ्यो निषादेभ्यश्च वो नमः.
transliteration: namaḥ senābhyaḥ senanibhyaśca vo namo nama ḥkṣattṛbhyaḥ saṁgrahītṛbhyaśca vo namo namastakṣabhyo rathakārebhyaśca vo namo nama ḥkulālebhyaḥ kamārebhyaśca vo namo nama ḥpuñjiṣṭebhyo niṣādebhyaśca vo namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) armies and army chiefs; prostration to Thee who art the trained charioteers and apprentices in chariot driving; prostration to Thee who art the carpenters and the chariot makers; prostration to Thee who art the potters and blacksmiths; prostration to Thee who art the fowlers and the fishermen.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) armies and army chiefs; prostration to Thee who art the trained charioteers and apprentices in chariot driving; prostration to Thee who art the carpenters and the chariot makers; prostration to Thee who art the potters and blacksmiths; prostration to Thee who art the fowlers and the fishermen.

sanskrit_shloka: नम इषुकृद्भ्यो धन्वकृद्भ्यश्च वो नमो नमो म्रुगयुभ्य ःश्वनिभ्यश्च वो नमो नम ःश्वभ्यः श्वपतिभ्यश्च वो नमः.
transliteration: nama iṣukṛdbhyo dhanvakṛdbhyaśca vo namo namo mrugayubhya ḥśvanibhyaśca vo namo nama ḥśvabhyaḥ śvapatibhyaśca vo namaḥ.
translation: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) the artisans who make arrows and bows; prostration to Thee who art the hunters and the huntsmen; prostration to Thee who art the hounds and the keepers of hounds.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Thee who art (in the form of) the artisans who make arrows and bows; prostration to Thee who art the hunters and the huntsmen; prostration to Thee who art the hounds and the keepers of hounds.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो भवाय च रुद्राय च नमः शर्वाय च प शुपतये च नमो नीलग्रीवाय च शितिकण्ठाय च नम ःकपर्दिने च व्युप्तकेशाय च नमः सहस्र् आक्षाय च शतधन्वने च.
transliteration: namo bhavāya ca rudrāya ca namaḥ śarvāya ca pa śupataye ca namo nīlagrīvāya ca śitikaṇṭhāya ca nama ḥkapardine ca vyuptakeśāya ca namaḥ sahasr ākṣāya ca śatadhanvane ca.
translation: Prostration to the Creator and Destroyer of the Universe; prostration to the Remover of sins and the Protector of all beings; prostration to the blue-necked One and the fair-necked One; prostration to the matted-locked One and the clean-shaven One; prostration to the thousand-eyed One and Him who wields multiple bows. Note:—“In the form of an austere mendicant, Siva is matted-locked; as a sannyasin, He is clean- shaven; as Indra, He is thousand-eyed; in His multiformed manifestation, He holds numberless bows,” says Sayana.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Creator and Destroyer of the Universe; prostration to the Remover of sins and the Protector of all beings; prostration to the blue-necked One and the fair-necked One; prostration to the matted-locked One and the clean-shaven One; prostration to the thousand-eyed One and Him who wields multiple bows. Note:—“In the form of an austere mendicant, Siva is matted-locked; as a sannyasin, He is clean- shaven; as Indra, He is thousand-eyed; in His multiformed manifestation, He holds numberless bows,” says Sayana.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो गिरिशाय च शिपिविष्टाय च नमो मीढुष्टमाय चे षुमते च नमो ह्रस्वाय च वामनाय च नमो ब् ऋहते च वर्षीयसे च नमो वृद्धाय च सꣳवृद्ध्वने च.
transliteration: namo giriśāya ca śipiviṣṭāya ca namo mīḍhuṣṭamāya ce ṣumate ca namo hrasvāya ca vāmanāya ca namo b ṛhate ca varṣīyase ca namo vṛddhāya ca saṁvṛddhvane ca.
translation: Prostration to the Resident of the mountains (as Siva) and the Immanent One in all beings (as Vishnu); prostration to the One who wields arrows and rains heavily through the clouds; prostration to the One who is dwarfed in size and small in limbs; prostration to the One who is huge in size and multi-formed in limbs; prostration to the Ancient One who is glorified through eternity.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Resident of the mountains (as Siva) and the Immanent One in all beings (as Vishnu); prostration to the One who wields arrows and rains heavily through the clouds; prostration to the One who is dwarfed in size and small in limbs; prostration to the One who is huge in size and multi-formed in limbs; prostration to the Ancient One who is glorified through eternity.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो अग्रियाय च प्रथमाय च नम आशवे चाजिराय च नम ःशीघ्रियाय च शीभ्याय च नम ऊर्म्याय च् आवस्वन्याय च नमः स्रोतस्याय च द्वीप्याय च.
transliteration: namo agriyāya ca prathamāya ca nama āśave cājirāya ca nama ḥśīghriyāya ca śībhyāya ca nama ūrmyāya c āvasvanyāya ca namaḥ srotasyāya ca dvīpyāya ca.
translation: Prostration to the Primeval One and the Chief of beings; prostration to the Omnipresent One and the agile among things; prostration to the One in the quick and the flowing; prostration to the One in the roaring waves and the still water; prostration to the One in the swift rivers and the islands.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Primeval One and the Chief of beings; prostration to the Omnipresent One and the agile among things; prostration to the One in the quick and the flowing; prostration to the One in the roaring waves and the still water; prostration to the One in the swift rivers and the islands.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो ज्येष्ठाय च कनिष्ठाय च नमः पूर्वजाय च् आपरजाय च नमो मध्यमाय चापगल्भाय च नमो जघन्य् आय च बुध्नियाय च नमः सोभ्य् आय च प्रतिसर्याय च.
transliteration: namo jyeṣṭhāya ca kaniṣṭhāya ca namaḥ pūrvajāya c āparajāya ca namo madhyamāya cāpagalbhāya ca namo jaghany āya ca budhniyāya ca namaḥ sobhy āya ca pratisaryāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is the eldest as well as the youngest; prostration to Him who is the Ancient Being as well as all that emanates from It; prostration to Him who is the middling creation (such as the celestials, etc.) as well as the infant; prostration to Him who is the last in creation (e.g. the animals, birds, etc.) as well as the trees and plants with their branches and foliage; prostration to Him who is mixed in character (e.g. virtue and vice, representing the human beings), as well as all that is moving.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is the eldest as well as the youngest; prostration to Him who is the Ancient Being as well as all that emanates from It; prostration to Him who is the middling creation (such as the celestials, etc.) as well as the infant; prostration to Him who is the last in creation (e.g. the animals, birds, etc.) as well as the trees and plants with their branches and foliage; prostration to Him who is mixed in character (e.g. virtue and vice, representing the human beings), as well as all that is moving.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो याम्याय च क्षेम्याय च नम उर्वर्याय च खल्य् आय च नमः श्लोक्याय चावसान्याय च नमो वन्य् आय च कक्श्याय च नमः श्रवाय च प्रति श्रवाय च.
transliteration: namo yāmyāya ca kṣemyāya ca nama urvaryāya ca khaly āya ca namaḥ ślokyāya cāvasānyāya ca namo vany āya ca kakśyāya ca namaḥ śravāya ca prati śravāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who dispenses justice as Yama (Lord of Death) and bestows the beatitude of salvation to beings; prostration to Him who reigns over the green earth rich with harvest and is in the farm yards; prostration to Him who is in the (mantras of the) Vedas and the (meditations of the) Upanishads; prostration to Him who is in the form of trees in forests and in creepers and plants; prostration to Him who is in sound and its echo.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who dispenses justice as Yama (Lord of Death) and bestows the beatitude of salvation to beings; prostration to Him who reigns over the green earth rich with harvest and is in the farm yards; prostration to Him who is in the (mantras of the) Vedas and the (meditations of the) Upanishads; prostration to Him who is in the form of trees in forests and in creepers and plants; prostration to Him who is in sound and its echo.

sanskrit_shloka: नम आशुषेणाय चाशुरथाय च नमः शूराय चावभिन्दते च नमो वर्मिणे च वरूथिने च नमो बिल्मिने च कवचिने च नम ःश्रुताय च श्रुतसेनाय च.
transliteration: nama āśuṣeṇāya cāśurathāya ca namaḥ śūrāya cāvabhindate ca namo varmiṇe ca varūthine ca namo bilmine ca kavacine ca nama ḥśrutāya ca śrutasenāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in armies moving fast and in chariots rattling forth; prostration to Him who is valiant and destroys enemies; prostration to Him who wields a shield and leads the hosts (to success); prostration to Him who is helmeted and armoured; prostration to Him who is renowned (Ancient One) and whose forces are reputed (in all creation.)

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in armies moving fast and in chariots rattling forth; prostration to Him who is valiant and destroys enemies; prostration to Him who wields a shield and leads the hosts (to success); prostration to Him who is helmeted and armoured; prostration to Him who is renowned (Ancient One) and whose forces are reputed (in all creation.)

sanskrit_shloka: नमो दुन्दुभ्याय चाहनन्याय च नमो धृष्णवे च प्रमृशाय च नमो दूताय च प्रहिताय च नमो निषङ्गिणे चेषुधिमते च.
transliteration: namo dundubhyāya cāhananyāya ca namo dhṛṣṇave ca pramṛśāya ca namo dūtāya ca prahitāya ca namo niṣaṅgiṇe ceṣudhimate ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is immanent in the sound of the drum and in the sound of the tabour; prostration to Him who is in those that never retreat in war and in the ablest reconnoitres; prostration to Him who is in the spies and in military messengers; prostration to Him who is in the wielders of swords and in the operators of the quiver.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is immanent in the sound of the drum and in the sound of the tabour; prostration to Him who is in those that never retreat in war and in the ablest reconnoitres; prostration to Him who is in the spies and in military messengers; prostration to Him who is in the wielders of swords and in the operators of the quiver.

sanskrit_shloka: नमस्तीक्ष्णेषवे चायुधिने च नमः स्वायुधाय च सुधन्वने च नमः स्रुत्याय च पथ्याय च नमः काट्याय च नीप्याय च.
transliteration: namastīkṣṇeṣave cāyudhine ca namaḥ svāyudhāya ca sudhanvane ca namaḥ srutyāya ca pathyāya ca namaḥ kāṭyāya ca nīpyāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who uses sharp arrows and countless weapons; prostration to Him who wields the auspicious missile (trident) and the blessed bow (called Pinaka); prostration to Him who is in narrow lanes and in broad highways; prostration to Him who is in dribbling streams and in mountain torrents of water.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who uses sharp arrows and countless weapons; prostration to Him who wields the auspicious missile (trident) and the blessed bow (called Pinaka); prostration to Him who is in narrow lanes and in broad highways; prostration to Him who is in dribbling streams and in mountain torrents of water.

sanskrit_shloka: नमः सूद्याय च सरस्याय च नमो नाद्याय च वैशन्ताय च नमः कूप्याय चावट्याय च नमो वर्ष्याय चावर्ष्याय च नमो मेघ्याय च विद्युत्याय च.
transliteration: namaḥ sūdyāya ca sarasyāya ca namo nādyāya ca vaiśantāya ca namaḥ kūpyāya cāvaṭyāya ca namo varṣyāya cāvarṣyāya ca namo meghyāya ca vidyutyāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in marshes and lakes; prostration to Him who is in rivers and reservoirs; prostration to Him who is in wells and pits; prostration to Him who is in rain and in oceans; prostration to Him who is in the clouds and in lightning.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in marshes and lakes; prostration to Him who is in rivers and reservoirs; prostration to Him who is in wells and pits; prostration to Him who is in rain and in oceans; prostration to Him who is in the clouds and in lightning.

sanskrit_shloka: नम ईध्रियाय चातप्याय च नमो वात्याय च रेष्मियाय च नमो वास्तव्याय च वास्तुपाय च.
transliteration: nama īdhriyāya cātapyāya ca namo vātyāya ca reṣmiyāya ca namo vāstavyāya ca vāstupāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in the autumnal clouds and in the heating sun; prostration to Him who is in the winds and in the stormy downpour of the deluge; prostration to Him who is in the wealth of cattle and of land.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in the autumnal clouds and in the heating sun; prostration to Him who is in the winds and in the stormy downpour of the deluge; prostration to Him who is in the wealth of cattle and of land.

sanskrit_shloka: नमः सोमाय च रुद्राय च नमस्ताम्राय चारुणाय च नमः शङ्गाय च पशुपतये च नम उग्राय च भीमाय च.
transliteration: namaḥ somāya ca rudrāya ca namastāmrāya cāruṇāya ca namaḥ śaṅgāya ca paśupataye ca nama ugrāya ca bhīmāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who has Uma as His consort and who causes to flee all sorrows (of samsara); prostration to Him who is crimson-coloured (as the rising sun) and is reddish (as the sun risen above the horizon); prostration to Him who brings about the peace (and happiness) of beings and protects all creatures; prostration to Him who is terrible (to foes) and fearful (to those who oppose Him).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who has Uma as His consort and who causes to flee all sorrows (of samsara); prostration to Him who is crimson-coloured (as the rising sun) and is reddish (as the sun risen above the horizon); prostration to Him who brings about the peace (and happiness) of beings and protects all creatures; prostration to Him who is terrible (to foes) and fearful (to those who oppose Him).

sanskrit_shloka: नमो अग्रेवधाय च दूरेवधाय च नमो हन्त्रे च हनीयसे च नमो वृक्षेभ्यो हरिकेशेभ्यो नमस्ताराय.
transliteration: namo agrevadhāya ca dūrevadhāya ca namo hantre ca hanīyase ca namo vṛkṣebhyo harikeśebhyo namastārāya.
translation: Prostration to Him who destroys enemies in front and who destroys them from behind; prostration to Him who is the Destroyer of things here and the Destroyer of everything in the end; prostration to Him who is in the form of trees filled with green leaves; prostration to Him who is embodied in Om (Pranava).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who destroys enemies in front and who destroys them from behind; prostration to Him who is the Destroyer of things here and the Destroyer of everything in the end; prostration to Him who is in the form of trees filled with green leaves; prostration to Him who is embodied in Om (Pranava).

sanskrit_shloka: नमश्शꣳभवे च मयोभवे च नमः शꣳकराय च मयस्कराय च नमः शिवाय च शिवतराय च.
transliteration: namaśśaṁbhave ca mayobhave ca namaḥ śaṁkarāya ca mayaskarāya ca namaḥ śivāya ca śivatarāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is the source of bliss, spiritual as well as temporal; prostration to Him who dispenses all happiness, heavenly as well as earthly; prostration to Him who is the Auspicious One, and is more auspicious than anything else.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is the source of bliss, spiritual as well as temporal; prostration to Him who dispenses all happiness, heavenly as well as earthly; prostration to Him who is the Auspicious One, and is more auspicious than anything else.

sanskrit_shloka: नमस्तीर्थ्याय च कूल्याय च नमः पार्याय चावार्याय च नमः प्रतरणाय चोत्तरणाय च नम आतार्याय चालाद्याय च नमः शष्प्याय च फेन्याय च नमः सिकत्याय च प्रवाह्याय च.
transliteration: namastīrthyāya ca kūlyāya ca namaḥ pāryāya cāvāryāya ca namaḥ prataraṇāya cottaraṇāya ca nama ātāryāya cālādyāya ca namaḥ śaṣpyāya ca phenyāya ca namaḥ sikatyāya ca pravāhyāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in the holy waters of shrines and in emblems erected on their banks; prostration to Him who is on this shore (as the bestower of prosperity) and on the other shore (as the blessedness beyond mortality); prostration to Him who is the means to cross over sin by ritual as well as by knowledge; prostration to Him who is the cause of rebirths and the fact behind the experiences of the fruits of karma; prostration to Him who is in the tender grass and in the fleeting foam; prostration to Him who is in the sands and the flowing waters (of rivers).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in the holy waters of shrines and in emblems erected on their banks; prostration to Him who is on this shore (as the bestower of prosperity) and on the other shore (as the blessedness beyond mortality); prostration to Him who is the means to cross over sin by ritual as well as by knowledge; prostration to Him who is the cause of rebirths and the fact behind the experiences of the fruits of karma; prostration to Him who is in the tender grass and in the fleeting foam; prostration to Him who is in the sands and the flowing waters (of rivers).

sanskrit_shloka: नम इरिण्याय च प्रपथ्याय च नमः किगीशिलाय च क्षयणाय च नमः कपर्दिने च पुलस्तये च नमो गोष्ठ्याय च गृह्याय च नमस्तल्प्याय च गेह्याय च नमः काट्याय च गह्वरेष्ठाय च नमो हृदय्याय च निवेष्प्याय च.
transliteration: nama iriṇyāya ca prapathyāya ca namaḥ kigïśilāya ca kṣayaṇāya ca namaḥ kapardine ca pulastaye ca namo goṣṭhyāya ca gṛhyāya ca namastalpyāya ca gehyāya ca namaḥ kāṭyāya ca gahvareṣṭhāya ca namo hṛdayyāya ca niveṣpyāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in fertile lands and in broad highroads; prostration to Him who is in rocky ground and in habitable places; prostration to Him who has matted locks and who reveals Himself to devotees; prostration to Him who is in cowsheds and in homes of people; prostration to Him who is in bedsteads and in palaces; prostration to Him who is in thorny jungles and in mountain caves; prostration to Him who is in whirlpools and in dewdrops.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in fertile lands and in broad highroads; prostration to Him who is in rocky ground and in habitable places; prostration to Him who has matted locks and who reveals Himself to devotees; prostration to Him who is in cowsheds and in homes of people; prostration to Him who is in bedsteads and in palaces; prostration to Him who is in thorny jungles and in mountain caves; prostration to Him who is in whirlpools and in dewdrops.

sanskrit_shloka: नमः पागीसव्याय च रजस्याय च नमः शुष्क्याय च हरित्याय च नमो लोप्याय चोलप्याय च नम ऊर्व्याय च सूर्म्याय च.
transliteration: namaḥ pāgïsavyāya ca rajasyāya ca namaḥ śuṣkyāya ca harityāya ca namo lopyāya colapyāya ca nama ūrvyāya ca sūrmyāya ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in atoms and in dust; prostration to Him who is in what is dry and what is green; prostration to Him who is in rugged terrain and in the green grass; prostration to Him who is in the earth and in the gallant-waved rivers.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in atoms and in dust; prostration to Him who is in what is dry and what is green; prostration to Him who is in rugged terrain and in the green grass; prostration to Him who is in the earth and in the gallant-waved rivers.

sanskrit_shloka: नमः पर्ण्याय च पर्णशद्याय च नमोऽपगुरमाणाय चाभिघ्नते च नम आख्खिदते च प्रख्खिदते च.
transliteration: namaḥ parṇyāya ca parṇaśadyāya ca namo'paguramāṇāya cābhighnate ca nama ākhkhidate ca prakhkhidate ca.
translation: Prostration to Him who is in fresh leaves and in heaps of dry leaves; prostration to Him who is with uplifted weapons and who strikes (the sinful); prostration to Him who afflicts (enemies) mildly as well as severely.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to Him who is in fresh leaves and in heaps of dry leaves; prostration to Him who is with uplifted weapons and who strikes (the sinful); prostration to Him who afflicts (enemies) mildly as well as severely.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो वः किरिकेभ्यो देवानागीहृदयेभ्यो नमो विक्षीणकेभ्यो नमो विचिन्वत्केभ्यो नम आनिर्हतेभ्यो नम आमीवत्केभ्यः.
transliteration: namo vaḥ kirikebhyo devānāgïhṛdayebhyo namo vikṣīṇakebhyo namo vicinvatkebhyo nama ānirhatebhyo nama āmīvatkebhyaḥ.
translation: Prostration to You all who are the hearts of the gods, bestowing on devotees wealth (material as well as spiritual); prostration to You who are undecaying; prostration to You who grants the wishes of everyone; prostration to You who destroys evil from all sides; prostration to You who manifests Yourself abundantly.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to You all who are the hearts of the gods, bestowing on devotees wealth (material as well as spiritual); prostration to You who are undecaying; prostration to You who grants the wishes of everyone; prostration to You who destroys evil from all sides; prostration to You who manifests Yourself abundantly.

sanskrit_shloka: द्रापे अन्धसस्पते दरिद्रन्नीललोहित, एषाꣳ पुरुषाणामेषाꣳ पशूनाꣳ मा भेर्माऽरो मो एषाꣳ किꣳ चनाममत्.
transliteration: drāpe andhasaspate daridrannīlalohita, eṣāṁ puruṣāṇāmeṣāṁ paśūnāṁ mā bhermā'ro mo eṣāṁ kiṁ canāmamat.
translation: O Wielder of the rod of justice (Punisher)! O Lord of food! O Unattached Independent One (possessing nothing)! O Blue and Red One in hue! May there not be fear in these people and these cattle (of ours)! May not any one of them stray away (or perish)! May not any one of them be diseased!

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: O Wielder of the rod of justice (Punisher)! O Lord of food! O Unattached Independent One (possessing nothing)! O Blue and Red One in hue! May there not be fear in these people and these cattle (of ours)! May not any one of them stray away (or perish)! May not any one of them be diseased!

sanskrit_shloka: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूह् शिवा विश्वाह भेषजी, शिवा रुद्रस्य भेषजी तया नो मृड जीवसे.
transliteration: yā te rudra śivā tanūh śivā viśvāha bheṣajī, śivā rudrasya bheṣajī tayā no mṛḍa jīvase.
translation: Rudra! That which is your auspicious form, auspicious as the universal panacea for all ills, auspicious as the bestower of (knowledge and realisation of) Your Rudra form—with that make us live in happiness.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Rudra! That which is your auspicious form, auspicious as the universal panacea for all ills, auspicious as the bestower of (knowledge and realisation of) Your Rudra form—with that make us live in happiness.

sanskrit_shloka: इमागीरुद्राय तवसे कपर्दिने क्षयद्वीराय प्रभरामहे मतिम्, यथा नः शमसद्द्विपदे चतुष्पदे विश्वꣳ पुष्टꣳ ग्रामे आस्मिन् अनातुरम्.
transliteration: imāgïrudrāya tavase kapardine kṣayadvīrāya prabharāmahe matim, yathā naḥ śamasaddvipade catuṣpade viśvaṁ puṣṭaṁ grāme āsmin anāturam.
translation: We dedicate this mind of ours to Rudra, the powerful, with matted hair, causing the waning (and destruction) of enemies, so that in this our locality (village, land or country) happiness may prevail on humankind and cattle, and all living beings may remain robust and free from troubles of any kind.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: We dedicate this mind of ours to Rudra, the powerful, with matted hair, causing the waning (and destruction) of enemies, so that in this our locality (village, land or country) happiness may prevail on humankind and cattle, and all living beings may remain robust and free from troubles of any kind.

sanskrit_shloka: मृडा नो रुद्रोत नो मयस्कृधि क्षयद्वीराय नमसा विधेम तेय्, यच्छꣳ च योश्च मनुरायजे पिता तदश्याम तव रुद्र प्रणीतौ.
transliteration: mṛḍā no rudrota no mayaskṛdhi kṣayadvīrāya namasā vidhema tey, yacchaṁ ca yośca manurāyaje pitā tadaśyāma tava rudra praṇītau.
translation: Rudra! Render us happy (both) here (with material prosperity) and in the hereafter (with spiritual blessedness); with our obeisance we propitiate You, the Destroyer of our enemies (internal and external); may we attain, Rudra, with Your loving Grace, all that happiness and freedom from sorrow which our father, Manu, acquired.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Rudra! Render us happy (both) here (with material prosperity) and in the hereafter (with spiritual blessedness); with our obeisance we propitiate You, the Destroyer of our enemies (internal and external); may we attain, Rudra, with Your loving Grace, all that happiness and freedom from sorrow which our father, Manu, acquired.

sanskrit_shloka: मा नो महान्तमुत मा नो अर्भकꣳ मा न उक्षन्त-मुत मा न उक्षितम्, मा नोऽवधीः पितरꣳ मोत मातरꣳ प्रिया मा नस्तनुवः रुद्ररीरिषः.
transliteration: mā no mahāntamuta mā no arbhakaṁ mā na ukṣanta-muta mā na ukṣitam, mā no'vadhīḥ pitaraṁ mota mātaraṁ priyā mā nastanuvaḥ rudrarīriṣaḥ.
translation: Rudra! Destroy not our aged ones or our young ones, our infants or our babes in the womb; kill not our father or our mother, or our dear bodies.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Rudra! Destroy not our aged ones or our young ones, our infants or our babes in the womb; kill not our father or our mother, or our dear bodies.

sanskrit_shloka: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयुषि मा नो गोषु मा नो अश्वेषु रीरिषः, वीरान्मा नो रुद्र भामितोऽवधीर्-हविष्मन्तो नमसा विधेम ते.
transliteration: mā nastoke tanaye mā na āyuṣi mā no goṣu mā no aśveṣu rīriṣaḥ, vīrānmā no rudra bhāmito'vadhīr-haviṣmanto namasā vidhema te.
translation: Rudra! Do not, in Your anger, bring trouble on our children, our sons, our lifespan, our cattle, our horses; destroy not our brave (useful) servants; we propitiate You with (our) prostrations, offering oblations (to You).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Rudra! Do not, in Your anger, bring trouble on our children, our sons, our lifespan, our cattle, our horses; destroy not our brave (useful) servants; we propitiate You with (our) prostrations, offering oblations (to You).

sanskrit_shloka: आरात्ते गोघ्न उत पूरुषघ्ने क्षयद्वीराय सुम्नमस्मे ते अस्तु, रक्षा च नो अधि च देव ब्रूह्यथा च नः शर्म यच्छद्विबर्हाः.
transliteration: ārātte goghna uta pūruṣaghne kṣayadvīrāya sumnamasme te astu, rakṣā ca no adhi ca deva brūhyathā ca naḥ śarma yacchadvibarhāḥ.
translation: God! Let Thy gentle form, meant for our good, which spells destruction on cattle and human beings in the enemy’s fighting forces, be near us; protect us, exalt us (among all things) and confer grace on us—Thou the glory of here and hereafter.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: God! Let Thy gentle form, meant for our good, which spells destruction on cattle and human beings in the enemy’s fighting forces, be near us; protect us, exalt us (among all things) and confer grace on us—Thou the glory of here and hereafter.

sanskrit_shloka: स्तुहि श्रुतꣳ गर्तसदꣳ युवानꣳ मृगन्न भीम-मुपहत्नुमुग्रम्, म्रुडा जरित्रे रुद्र स्तवानो अन्यन्ते अस्मन्निवपन्तु सेनाः.
transliteration: stuhi śrutaṁ gartasadaṁ yuvānaṁ mṛganna bhīma-mupahatnumugram, mruḍā jaritre rudra stavāno anyante asmannivapantu senāḥ.
translation: Praise the celebrated One; the Dweller in the cave (of the heart); ever young (new and fresh); terrible at the time of destruction (of enemies and of the universe in the end), like a ferocious lion. O Rudra, make us, praying through this mortal frame, happy. Let Thy forces (armies) wipe out what is different from us (our foes).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Praise the celebrated One; the Dweller in the cave (of the heart); ever young (new and fresh); terrible at the time of destruction (of enemies and of the universe in the end), like a ferocious lion. O Rudra, make us, praying through this mortal frame, happy. Let Thy forces (armies) wipe out what is different from us (our foes).

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—This is a prayer for the success of oneself over one’s enemies, external as well as internal. What is different from us is what is other than the true Self or Atman.

sanskrit_shloka: परिणो रुद्रस्य हेतिर्वृणक्तु परि त्वेषस्य दुर्मतिरघायोः, अव स्थिरा मघवद्भ्यस्तनुष्व मीढ्वस्तोकाय तनयाय म्रुडय.
transliteration: pariṇo rudrasya hetirvṛṇaktu pari tveṣasya durmatiraghāyoḥ, ava sthirā maghavadbhyastanuṣva mīḍhvastokāya tanayāya mruḍaya.
translation: May the destructive weapon of Rudra, as also His burning angry will risen against sinners, keep away from us (not harm us). O Granter of boons to those who surrender themselves with offerings! Turn away Your wrath from us, who are prostrate before You. Bestow happiness on our children and grandchildren.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: May the destructive weapon of Rudra, as also His burning angry will risen against sinners, keep away from us (not harm us). O Granter of boons to those who surrender themselves with offerings! Turn away Your wrath from us, who are prostrate before You. Bestow happiness on our children and grandchildren.

sanskrit_shloka: मीढुष्टम शिवतम शिवो नः सुमना भव, परमे व्रुक्श आयुधꣳ निधाय कृत्तिꣳ वसान आचर पिनाकꣳ बिभ्रदागहि.
transliteration: mīḍhuṣṭama śivatama śivo naḥ sumanā bhava, parame vrukśa āyudhaṁ nidhāya kṛttiṁ vasāna ācara pinākaṁ bibhradāgahi.
translation: O Supreme Bestower of blessings (on devotees)! O Supremely Auspicious One! Be propitious and graceful towards us. Leaving Thy destructive weapons behind on the top of a high tree, descend and appear before us wearing the tiger skin and wielding Thy Pinaka bow (merely as Thy insignia).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: O Supreme Bestower of blessings (on devotees)! O Supremely Auspicious One! Be propitious and graceful towards us. Leaving Thy destructive weapons behind on the top of a high tree, descend and appear before us wearing the tiger skin and wielding Thy Pinaka bow (merely as Thy insignia).

sanskrit_shloka: विकिरिद विलोहित नमस्ते अस्तु भगवः, यास्ते सहस्रगीहेतयोऽन्यमस्मन्निवपन्तु ताः.
transliteration: vikirida vilohita namaste astu bhagavaḥ, yāste sahasragïhetayo'nyamasmannivapantu tāḥ.
translation: O Profuse Granter of boons! O White-hued One! Prostration be to You, O Lord! May Your countless weapons, all of them, destroy what is different from us.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: O Profuse Granter of boons! O White-hued One! Prostration be to You, O Lord! May Your countless weapons, all of them, destroy what is different from us.

commentaries.author: Sayana Acharya Notes
commentaries.text: Note:—The above is a mantra to ward off anything that is contrary to self—disease, poverty, ignorance, enemies and, finally, the sense of separateness in Pure Being.

sanskrit_shloka: सहस्राणि सहस्रधा बाहुवोस्तव हेतयः, तासामीशानो भगवः पराचीना मुखा कृधि.
transliteration: sahasrāṇi sahasradhā bāhuvostava hetayaḥ, tāsāmīśāno bhagavaḥ parācīnā mukhā kṛdhi.
translation: Lord! In Your hands are myriad weapons of diverse types; You are master over them all. Condescend to turn their faces away from us.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Lord! In Your hands are myriad weapons of diverse types; You are master over them all. Condescend to turn their faces away from us.

sanskrit_shloka: सहस्राणि सहस्रशो ये रुद्रा अधि भूम्याम्, तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.
transliteration: sahasrāṇi sahasraśo ye rudrā adhi bhūmyām, teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.
translation: We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those myriad forms of the countless manifestations of Rudra, who range over this earth.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those myriad forms of the countless manifestations of Rudra, who range over this earth.

sanskrit_shloka: अस्मिन् महत्यर्णवेऽन्तरिक्षे भवा अधि, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि).
transliteration: asmin mahatyarṇave'ntarikṣe bhavā adhi, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi).
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms of Rudra who are spread over this vast ocean of space. being recited only once after nine half-verses beginning with the present one. We shall, however, insert the same with every half-verse to make the sentence complete and the sense clear.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms of Rudra who are spread over this vast ocean of space. being recited only once after nine half-verses beginning with the present one. We shall, however, insert the same with every half-verse to make the sentence complete and the sense clear.

sanskrit_shloka: नीलग्रीवाशितिकण्ठाः शर्वा अधः क्षमाचराः, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: nīlagrīvāśitikaṇṭhāḥ śarvā adhaḥ kṣamācarāḥ, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms characterised by blue necks and also fair necks, the Sarvas (manifestations of Rudra) who wander in the nether regions (as their lords).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms characterised by blue necks and also fair necks, the Sarvas (manifestations of Rudra) who wander in the nether regions (as their lords).

sanskrit_shloka: नीलग्रीवाश्शितिकण्ठा दिवगीरुद्रा उपश्रिताः, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: nīlagrīvāśśitikaṇṭhā divagïrudrā upaśritāḥ, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms characterised by blue necks and also fair necks, the Rudras who reign over the heavenly regions (as their lords).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms characterised by blue necks and also fair necks, the Rudras who reign over the heavenly regions (as their lords).

sanskrit_shloka: ये वृक्शेषु सस्पिꣳजरा नीलग्रीवा विलोहिताः, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: ye vṛkśeṣu saspiṁjarā nīlagrīvā vilohitāḥ, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms who, with yellow hues, like tender grass, and with blue necks, also sometimes with reddish colour, reside in trees (as their lords).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms who, with yellow hues, like tender grass, and with blue necks, also sometimes with reddish colour, reside in trees (as their lords).

sanskrit_shloka: ये भूतानामधिपतयो विशिखासः कपर्दिनः, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: ye bhūtānāmadhipatayo viśikhāsaḥ kapardinaḥ, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) lords of ghostly spirits, some of whom are shaven-headed and some of whom have matted hair.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) lords of ghostly spirits, some of whom are shaven-headed and some of whom have matted hair.

sanskrit_shloka: ये अन्नेषु विविध्यन्ति पात्रेषु पिबतो जनान्, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: ye anneṣu vividhyanti pātreṣu pibato janān, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms of Rudra who afflict (people) through food (by way of imbalance of the humours, etc.) and (afflict) those who drink in vessels (by sips and excesses, etc.)

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) forms of Rudra who afflict (people) through food (by way of imbalance of the humours, etc.) and (afflict) those who drink in vessels (by sips and excesses, etc.)

sanskrit_shloka: ये पथाꣳ पथिरक्शय ऐलबृदा यव्युधः, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: ye pathāṁ pathirakśaya ailabṛdā yavyudhaḥ, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) who are the protectors of all the paths (of the soul, both here and hereafter), who control the supply of foodstuffs (to all beings), who fight with and drive away enemies (who stand in our way).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) who are the protectors of all the paths (of the soul, both here and hereafter), who control the supply of foodstuffs (to all beings), who fight with and drive away enemies (who stand in our way).

sanskrit_shloka: ये तीर्थानि प्रचरन्ति सृकावन्तो निषङ्गिणः, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: ye tīrthāni pracaranti sṛkāvanto niṣaṅgiṇaḥ, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) who stalk about (in holy places to protect them) with sharp swords and fierce instruments (in their hands).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: (We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of those) who stalk about (in holy places to protect them) with sharp swords and fierce instruments (in their hands).

sanskrit_shloka: य एतावन्तश्च भूयागीसश्च दिशो रुद्रा वितस्थिरे, (तेषागीसहस्रयोजनेऽवधन्वानि तन्मसि.)
transliteration: ya etāvantaśca bhūyāgïsaśca diśo rudrā vitasthire, (teṣāgïsahasrayojane'vadhanvāni tanmasi.)
translation: We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of all these forms of Rudra, and many more (than already mentioned), who exist filling the quarters.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: We keep unstringed, a thousand leagues away, the bows of all these forms of Rudra, and many more (than already mentioned), who exist filling the quarters.

sanskrit_shloka: नमो रुद्रेभ्यो ये पृथिव्याꣳ येऽन्तरिक्शे ये दिवि येषामन्नꣳ वातो वर्षमिषवस्तेभ्यो दश प्राचीर्दश दक्षिणा दश प्रतीचीर्दशोदीचीर्दशोर्ध्वास्तेभ्यो नमस्ते नो मृडयन्तु ते यꣳ द्विष्मो यश्च नो द्वेष्टि तꣳ वो जम्भे दधामि.
transliteration: namo rudrebhyo ye pṛthivyāṁ ye'ntarikśe ye divi yeṣāmannaṁ vāto varṣamiṣavastebhyo daśa prācīrdaśa dakṣiṇā daśa pratīcīrdaśodīcīrdaśordhvāstebhyo namaste no mṛḍayantu te yaṁ dviṣmo yaśca no dveṣṭi taṁ vo jambhe dadhāmi.
translation: Prostration to the Rudras (in myriad forms) who exist in earth atmosphere and heaven, and whose arrows (weapons) are food, wind and rain (respectively); prostration to these with folded hands, all the ten fingers joined forward in submission to the east, ten fingers thus to the south, ten fingers to the west, ten fingers to the north, ten fingers upwards; prostration to them. May they render us happy. Whomsoever we hate and whoever hates us, him we, having thus resorted, consign (O Rudras!) into your wide open mouths.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Prostration to the Rudras (in myriad forms) who exist in earth atmosphere and heaven, and whose arrows (weapons) are food, wind and rain (respectively); prostration to these with folded hands, all the ten fingers joined forward in submission to the east, ten fingers thus to the south, ten fingers to the west, ten fingers to the north, ten fingers upwards; prostration to them. May they render us happy. Whomsoever we hate and whoever hates us, him we, having thus resorted, consign (O Rudras!) into your wide open mouths.

sanskrit_shloka: त्र्यꣳबकꣳ यजामहे सुगन्धिꣳ पुष्टिवर्धनम्, उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान्मृत्योर्-मुक्शीय माऽमृतात्.
transliteration: tryaṁbakaṁ yajāmahe sugandhiṁ puṣṭivardhanam, urvārukamiva bandhanānmṛtyor-mukśīya mā'mṛtāt.
translation: We worship the Three-Eyed One, fragrant (with energy), increasing strength and prosperity (of those who adore Him); may I (we) be freed from death for (the sake of) immortality, as a cucumber is freed from its hold (of bondage to the creeper).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: We worship the Three-Eyed One, fragrant (with energy), increasing strength and prosperity (of those who adore Him); may I (we) be freed from death for (the sake of) immortality, as a cucumber is freed from its hold (of bondage to the creeper).

sanskrit_shloka: यो रुद्रोऽअग्नौ योऽअप्सु य ओषधीषु यो रुद्रो विश्वा भुवना विवेश तस्मै रुद्राय नमो अस्तु.
transliteration: yo rudro'agnau yo'apsu ya oṣadhīṣu yo rudro viśvā bhuvanā viveśa tasmai rudrāya namo astu.
translation: That Rudra who is in fire, who is in water, who is in (medical) herbs, that Rudra who has entered all the worlds—to that Rudra be prostration.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: That Rudra who is in fire, who is in water, who is in (medical) herbs, that Rudra who has entered all the worlds—to that Rudra be prostration.

sanskrit_shloka: तमु ष्टुहि यः स्विषुः सुधन्वा यो विश्वस्य क्शयति भेषजस्य, यक्श्वामहे सौमनसाय रुद्रꣳ नम्होभिर्देवमसुरꣳ दुवस्य.
transliteration: tamu ṣṭuhi yaḥ sviṣuḥ sudhanvā yo viśvasya kśayati bheṣajasya, yakśvāmahe saumanasāya rudraṁ namhobhirdevamasuraṁ duvasya.
translation: Resort to Him, who is armed with excellent arrows and a good bow, who is the source of all remedies for worldly ills; we worship (that) God, Rudra, the Destroyer of pains, with (our) salutations, for (attaining) peace of mind.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Resort to Him, who is armed with excellent arrows and a good bow, who is the source of all remedies for worldly ills; we worship (that) God, Rudra, the Destroyer of pains, with (our) salutations, for (attaining) peace of mind.

sanskrit_shloka: अयꣳ मे हस्तो भगवानयꣳ मे भगवत्तरः, अयꣳ मे विश्व-भेषजोऽयगीशिवाभिमर्शनः.
transliteration: ayaṁ me hasto bhagavānayaṁ me bhagavattaraḥ, ayaṁ me viśva-bheṣajo'yagïśivābhimarśanaḥ.
translation: This hand of mine is blessed; this, mine, is twice blessed; this, mine, is the remedy for the ills of all the world—this, which has touched Siva (in the shrine of worship).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: This hand of mine is blessed; this, mine, is twice blessed; this, mine, is the remedy for the ills of all the world—this, which has touched Siva (in the shrine of worship).

sanskrit_shloka: ये ते सहस्रमयुतꣳ पाशा मृत्यो मर्त्याय हन्तवे, तान् यज्ञस्य मायया सर्वानव यजामहे.
transliteration: ye te sahasramayutaṁ pāśā mṛtyo martyāya hantave, tān yajñasya māyayā sarvānava yajāmahe.
translation: O Destroyer (Death of death)! What thousands and tens of thousands of binding forces wielded by You there are, (which are) meant for the ruin of the mortal individual; those all we set aside with the power of sacrifice.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: O Destroyer (Death of death)! What thousands and tens of thousands of binding forces wielded by You there are, (which are) meant for the ruin of the mortal individual; those all we set aside with the power of sacrifice.

sanskrit_shloka: मृत्यवे स्वाहा मृत्यवे स्वाहा, ओꣳ नमो भगवते रुद्राय विष्णवे मृत्युर्मे पाहि.
transliteration: mṛtyave svāhā mṛtyave svāhā, ōṁ namo bhagavate rudrāya viṣṇave mṛtyurme pāhi.
translation: May this offering be to the Death Supreme (Death of death, or Destroyer of all evil, sin and sorrow)! May this offering be to the Death Supreme! Om, Prostration to the All-Pervading, Blessed Lord Rudra! Save me from death (mortal existence)!

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: May this offering be to the Death Supreme (Death of death, or Destroyer of all evil, sin and sorrow)! May this offering be to the Death Supreme! Om, Prostration to the All-Pervading, Blessed Lord Rudra! Save me from death (mortal existence)!

sanskrit_shloka: प्राणानाꣳ ग्रन्थिरसि रुद्रो मा विशान्तकः तेनान्नेनाप्यायस्व. ओꣳ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः.
transliteration: prāṇānāṁ granthirasi rudro mā viśāntakaḥ tenānnenāpyāyasva. ōṁ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ.
translation: Thou, Rudra, art the centre of the vital forces; enter not (therefore) as the destroyer. With this sustaining element (of Thy Grace), make us grow into abundance and fullness! Om. May there be Peace, Peace, Peace.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Thou, Rudra, art the centre of the vital forces; enter not (therefore) as the destroyer. With this sustaining element (of Thy Grace), make us grow into abundance and fullness! Om. May there be Peace, Peace, Peace.

sanskrit_shloka: ओꣳ तत्पुरुष्हय विद्महे महादेवाय धीमहि, तन्नो रुद्रः प्रछोदयात्.
transliteration: ōṁ tatpuruṣhaya vidmahe mahādevāya dhīmahi, tanno rudraḥ prachodayāt.
translation: We commune ourselves with that great Purusha, and meditate on Mahadeva (Great God). May that Rudra (Siva) direct us (to the Great Goal).

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: We commune ourselves with that great Purusha, and meditate on Mahadeva (Great God). May that Rudra (Siva) direct us (to the Great Goal).

sanskrit_shloka: ओꣳ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः.
transliteration: ōṁ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ.
translation: Om. May there be Peace, Peace, Peace.

translations.author: Standard English
translations.text: Om. May there be Peace, Peace, Peace.
